plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney DE + TF activity
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a small, clean human kidney bulk RNA-seq experiment: 12,000 genes x 12 samples, 6 aldosterone-treated vs 6 vehicle controls, unpaired, single batch, raw gene-level counts already summarized from Salmon. The question has two parts: which genes change (differential expression), and which transcription factors sit behind those changes (regulator activity). The plan runs the grounded procedure for this situation (n=6/group, counts, no batch confounding): blind sample-structure QC before any test; a minimal low-count pre-filter; median-of-ratios size factors inside the DESeq2 negative-binomial model with a Wald test, apeglm-shrunk fold changes and BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering; an edgeR quasi-likelihood run on the same counts as the second method, with the intersection reported as the high-confidence DE set; fgsea preranked GSEA on the full Wald-statistic-ranked list against MSigDB Hallmark and WikiPathways human; and decoupleR ulm TF activity on the Wald statistics of all tested genes against the CollecTRI human regulons (DoRothEA A-C as a signed alternative). Because counts are already gene-level and no transcript-level quantification files exist, the tximport length-offset step is not applicable — this limitation is stated in the report rather than silently dropped. Enrichment and TF-activity keys are HGNC symbols, matching the gene symbols in counts.csv and both GMT/regulon resources, so no cross-identifier mapping is needed; the unmapped share is still reported.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes
DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage
fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic with MSigDB Hallmark
Transcription factor activity with decoupleR ulm on the CollecTRI regulons
